mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, directly increasing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital for corporations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate increase above 5.5% for three consecutive months indicates labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand that accelerates corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved earnings outlooks.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing supply chain disruption (INDPRO growth below 0.5% monthly) during late-cycle expansions reduces corporate profitability through input cost inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO growth is below 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.5% for two consecutive months triggers market expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL signal an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that raises discount rates while inflation erodes real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint rise in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fails to produce negative 20-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 100k signals labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases by more than 100k monthly.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 annual growth above 2.5%), S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days as economic momentum peaks and monetary policy tightens to prevent overheating.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 annual growth exceeds 2.5%.
